whole‐body cryotherapy following severe intermittent running did not attenuate acute changes in inflammation, muscle damage, and stress.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of Whole‐body cryotherapy on the recovery from severe exercise stress in trained males.
the physiological and performance effects of Whole‐Body Cryotherapy (WCB) in athletes and non‐athletes.
the physiological and psychological effects of WBC on athletes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acute effects of WBC following severe intermittent running on biomarkers of muscle damage, stress and inflammation were not significant.
WBC following HIR exercise does not appear to have an acute anti‐inflammatory effect and that it may have a negative influence on subsequent exercise performance in trained individuals.
WBC does not improve exercise‐induced recovery in endurance‐trained males following severe intermittent running.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of WBC following HIR exercise does not appear to be a useful recovery modality.
WBC following severe intermittent running did not alter the acute inflammatory and muscle damage biomarkers and did not improve exercise recovery.
the use of WBC following HIR in trained athletes does not appear to have a significant impact on the recovery process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of WBC following high‐intensitity intermittent exercise is not recommended for the recovery of endurance athletes.
a single bout of WBC following HIR did not attenuate post‐exercise inflammatory or muscle damage responses.
a single WBC session is not sufficient to reduce exercise‐induced increases in inflammation, muscle damage, or stress.
